display.title: Mitzvah Time: Why We Say the Shema at Night and in the Morning
display.summary_short: A review of the kavanah of 'Echad', and why we say the Shema twice a day: the Torah says 'when you lie down and when you rise up'.
display.summary_long: A short Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi first reviews last week's lesson: the three letters of Echad remind us that Hashem is the one Master of the seven heavens, the earth and the four directions. He then explains why the Shema is said twice every day. The Torah says 'b'shochbecha uv'kumecha', when you lie down and when you rise up, so we say the Shema at night before going to sleep and again in the morning. These words appear in both the first and the second paragraphs of the Shema.
display.lesson: Say the Shema every night before sleep and every morning when you wake up, as the Torah commands.
